answer: In an agent marketplace selling timber, sonnet commissions, and trellis designs, voting power is proportional to tokens locked in escrow for 90 days, rather than the number of accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents gives the same total voting weight as staking them in one account. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital and forgoing other uses for it.
